_note: End-card slogans, one line under the LangX wordmark. 'speak' is the app's own onboarding headline (intro.slide1Title in apps/mobile/src/i18n/messages/*.ts), copied verbatim, so its eight translations already ship and the first screen after install says the same thing. The other two are new copy and want a native read before use. None claims a number, a result or a speed.

practice.why: Behic's line (23 Oct). Three beats; on the splash card each comma group rises in turn. Only en and tr are written; every other locale falls back to its 'speak' line.

speak.why: The exchange in four words: you teach your language, you practise theirs. Already the app's first onboarding slide in all eight locales.
speak.es: Habla el tuyo, practica el suyo
speak.fr: Parle la tienne, pratique la leur
speak.pt-BR: Fale a sua, pratique a deles

natives.why: The plainest true sentence: every match is a native speaker of what you are learning (the matching rule in intro.slide1Body). Clearest for someone who has never heard of LangX.

exchange.why: Names the category people search for (language exchange) and the difference from course and AI apps (a person on the other side).
exchange.es: Intercambio de idiomas, de tú a tú
exchange.pt-BR: Intercâmbio de idiomas, de pessoa para pessoa
exchange.ru: Языковой обмен — от человека к человеку
exchange.ar: تبادل لغوي من إنسان إلى إنسان
